title: Two tags of one image share one base rootfs slot, so any build's create rewrites the disk every other build boots from
foundBy: user report (host): Rishi Vaish, 2026-11-05, after a second session's create broke every staging on a shared host: "how do we not have the isolation we need?"
details:
`Cache.BaseRootfs` (internal/fcdisk/fcdisk.go) keys the cached base rootfs by image REPOSITORY, not by the reference: `base-rootfs-ghcr.io-codesweep-ai-sandbox.ext4` is one file for every tag of `ghcr.io/codesweep-ai/sandbox`. Its own comment says what follows: "Two tags of one repository still share a slot and rebuild in place when the stamp says the content moved." So two cs-sandbox builds pinned to different tags, both correct by their own pins, fight over one 32 GiB file: whichever runs `create` last rewrites it, silently, for everyone.

What happened on 2026-11-05, on a host with several agent sessions, each repo carrying its own pinned `tools/cs-sandbox`. One session built cs-sandbox v0.0.0-20260915174144-601626e43f70, whose image tag is of the same date. At 22:08:12Z it ran `tools/cs-sandbox create probe-sbx --group podcast ...`. The create found the shared slot stamped with another tag's content and rebuilt it in place from the 09-15 image (and replaced vmlinux.elf, initrd and modules.tar: kernel 6.19.10 for 7.2.5). The other sessions pin v0.0.0-20261025044344-a0df4c558d44. From that moment their own pre-flight image check refused every sandbox staging: the 09-15 image carries no python3 `jsonschema`, and its /tmp entries are root-owned. Three sessions' work stopped for an hour; a paid run about to start would have died at its first staging. The host was repaired by a pinned-binary create, which rebuilt the slot back (11 s), and the other repo repinned to the same tag.

Pinning callers does not cover this: the pin decides what each caller asks for, and the slot decides what every caller gets. The fix belongs where the shared state lives.

Two fixes, either closes it; the first is the isolation the design lacks, the second is the loud failure that should exist regardless:
1. Key the base rootfs by the whole reference (tag or digest): `base-rootfs-<repository>-<tag>.ext4`, one slot per image version in use. A create then finds exactly the rootfs its image made or builds its own, and never rewrites another's. Cost: one sparse 32 GiB file per version in use (5.9 GiB allocated for the shipped image); `cs-sandbox rm --prune` or a doctor hint can drop slots no instance references.
2. Refuse to rebuild a base rootfs in place when its stamp names another image, at least while any instance on the host was created from that slot. Simpler still: refuse always, unless an explicit `cs-sandbox build` asks for it. Print which image owns the file and stop. A stray build then fails on its own create instead of breaking everyone else's.

A regression test runs two Cache users with different tags of one repository. After both create, each boots the rootfs of its own image, with the stamp equal to its image id. The first's stamp is unchanged by the second's create.

notes.text: Commits 054d8f4 and aa53dce build both fixes. The base rootfs and its stamp are now keyed by the whole image reference, so two tags of one repository each keep their own. A repository-keyed file whose stamp names the same image is adopted by rename, and one stamped by another image is left alone. A create whose own slot carries another image's stamp refuses, naming both images and the explicit build that replaces it. Doctor lists every slot with its image, its allocated size and the sandboxes made from it, and prints the rm that drops the unused ones. Three new unit tests fail on 73a791a and pass on these commits. CI still has to show the smoke and integration tiers booting from the new slot names, since this host ran unit tests and static checks only.
